title: Tanzanian Lamb Pilau
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Pilau ya Kondoo — Zanzibar lamb pilau. Tender lamb slow-cooked in Zanzibar whole spices, its rich broth used to cook fragrant basmati rice to golden perfection. The grandest Eid ul-Adha dish of the Tanzanian coast.
longDesc: Lamb pilau is made specifically for Eid ul-Adha — the festival of sacrifice — when lamb is the celebratory meat. The full Zanzibar spice array, the patient slow simmer of the lamb, and the fragrant rice cooked in the spiced broth produce a dish of extraordinary significance and flavour.
steps: Toast and grind half the spices. Keep half whole.
Add garlic, ginger, spices, tomatoes. Cook 10 minutes.
Return lamb. Add 8 cups water. Simmer 60—75 minutes until very tender.
Remove lamb. Measure broth — need 7 cups.
Add rice to broth. Boil. Cover. Lowest heat 20 minutes.
Place lamb on top of rice for final steaming.
chefTips: See TZA025 for goat pilau technique — lamb pilau follows the same method.
Lamb broth is slightly milder than goat — use slightly more spice.
cookingScience: See TZA025 for pilau cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Eid lamb from local Tanzanian pastoral farmers.
culturalNote: Lamb pilau for Eid ul-Adha is the most significant food of Tanzania's Islamic calendar — the dish that marks the day of sacrifice and is shared with the community, the neighbours, and the less fortunate.
